title: Centered Fourier observation sum
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to the signs $\\{-1,1\\}$, and let $S$ be a subset of $\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$. For a positive integer $m$ and a sample $x_1,\\ldots,x_m$ in the cube, the sum of the centered Fourier observations equals $m$ times the difference between their empirical average and the Fourier coefficient: $\\sum_{j=1}^m (f(x_j)\\chi_S(x_j)-\\widehat f(S))=m(\\frac{1}{m}\\sum_{j=1}^m f(x_j)\\chi_S(x_j)-\\widehat f(S))$, where $\\chi_S$ is the monomial indexed by $S$ and $\\widehat f(S)$ is the uniform Fourier coefficient.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function from the cube to the signs
